colophon: Tiruchirrambalam: the holy Small Hall of Chidambaram, the closing salutation of Shaiva hymns.

lines.1: When fierce sorrow swells and surges and comes to crush you, O heart, do not shrink in fear,
lines.2: wasting to bone and drooping here: give that up! Without flagging, worship
lines.3: the Lord whose head holds the swelling, surging Ganga, and in the sky's midst, the white
lines.4: young moon with its growing horn, and the erukku flower: worship that Lord alone.
lines.5: Thinking, 'There is no Lord but him,'
lines.6: holding him in the heart with reverent awe, speaking of him,
lines.7: those who live without forgetting: on this earth, forever,
lines.8: the Lord guards them from being born again.
lines.9: Those who praise him for many days, calling him their Lord, and bow: seeing their sorrow
lines.10: he will not stand by. See, that Lord! Where swarms of bees dig in and
lines.11: jostle among the thick konrai blossoms, and there, lying hidden, the snake
lines.12: hisses in his matted locks: he is the Brahmin with the long crest of red gold.
lines.13: Those who took the Brahmin as their refuge and became his servants, he keeps from sinking:
lines.14: the mighty one comes, holds them close, guards and cherishes them. Gold set with clustered gems
lines.15: he will not wear even when he sees it, yet the deadly snake he wears:
lines.16: what more is there to see, O heart, from now on?
lines.17: Now, the one called Ganga in your long matted locks:
lines.18: if the mountain maiden with fruit-red lips, who shares your body, should see her, what will you do? With the bow in your hand,
lines.19: when the three cities of those who raged against you burned that day, sinking into red fire,
lines.20: you fitted one single long arrow: O our Shankara!
lines.21: Shankara, him of the low-hanging matted locks, who on those locks
lines.22: delighted to set the swelling serpent, the holy one, who on that one day
lines.23: will cry out, 'Alas, alas!' and keep us from sinking: always,
lines.24: without ceasing, O heart, speak of him.
lines.25: There is one thing to say, if you would hear it: the snake that hisses
lines.26: on your garland red as the evening sky, never touch it, you who have set the Ganga, streaming down
lines.27: and rolling in waves everywhere, and the honey-filled konrai, on your red matted locks,
lines.28: and the fragrant vanni leaves upon your head, O Brahmin of the Vedas.
lines.29: The Brahmin, the meaning of the Vedas,
lines.30: the source of the Vedas, the one whose holy day is Adirai: to fathom him,
lines.31: Vishnu, burrowing in as a mighty boar, could not reach him,
lines.32: and said, 'I cannot, sir,' there below.
lines.33: You who say, 'We would push back the sea of low sorrow's flood and, going deep within,
lines.34: not fall, but dwell in bliss': the hero who saw the cities of his foes
lines.35: laid waste, the eight-shouldered one, at his feet of fresh gold
lines.36: bow without delay, submit, and for all your days hold to them first.
lines.37: Having mastered the five that matter most, and humbled themselves,
lines.38: those who have understood the highest things will see the feet of red gold of the one of the highest
lines.39: heavens, the one of Adirai, whose throat darkened
lines.40: when he drank the halahala poison.
lines.41: Those who long to see his red feet with their anklets, and those who long to cherish them:
lines.42: at the mere sight of his shadow, their karma cannot stand. Unmatched,
lines.43: our Lord with the red body that blazes with fire's light: when it sees us strew great flowers from our hands
lines.44: in worship, can the ancient karma that clings to us and crushes us still stand?
lines.45: Before your ancient karma comes to surround you, without delay,
lines.46: bow quickly; the one who has the gentle one called Uma
lines.47: as his share, who burned up the very form of Death, who shines
lines.48: with sacred ash: think of him, O heart.
lines.49: Stop thinking, O heart, that there is any refuge here
lines.50: in your wife and your children, trusting in them. The one whose matted crest a river entered
lines.51: yet it is not wet, our Lord, our father, like a red fire that never dims,
lines.52: the Lord of the immortals, who dwells in the heavens: his feet are the refuge.
lines.53: That day, with the sole of your foot, the demon's twenty shoulders
lines.54: and ten heads you crushed: how was it done? On your head
lines.55: a river bathes you; you dance in the fire that is never quenched; in that fire's
lines.56: ash you bathe, and in ghee you bathe, you!
lines.57: Standing firm, how was it that the three great walled cities of the Danavas, all at once,
lines.58: burned where they stood in fire when you touched your bow? While the wailing, strong-mouthed
lines.59: ghouls stand and sing, with the vast burning-ground for your stage, you move in the dance,
lines.60: and dance on till the goblin hosts bow down: O holy one of the thronging anklets!
lines.61: The good deeds I have done, my not straying onto false paths,
lines.62: my five senses brought into accord by thought: all of it came from
lines.63: the love that made me a servant of the Lord who delighted to wrap his whole form
lines.64: in the flayed hide of the mighty elephant.
lines.65: How is he to be reached through love? Upon him a dancing serpent
lines.66: lets no one come near him, and not only that:
lines.67: he binds on strings of skulls that were once heads, and wears white
lines.68: bones as well, and delights to ride upon a bull!
lines.69: Has he nothing to ride but a bull, our Lord,
lines.70: whose shining matted locks all rivers flow into, who, when the gods
lines.71: gathered long ago, drank the poison of the broad sea, spat out by
lines.72: the hooded serpent? Has he nothing else to ride?
lines.73: To us who have always done him sweet service, if one day he
lines.74: would speak one word to us, would that be his grace? Unmatched,
lines.75: the white bull that carries him: having searched for one to equal it for fruit-lipped
lines.76: Uma and found none, he simply took her up with him: O noblest one!
lines.77: When those who lived as fine people die, before their kin
lines.78: can stack the dead wood and set it alight, the Noblest One,
lines.79: who drank the poison of the vast ocean, who bathes in ghee: hear of his greatness,
lines.80: O heart as deep as the sea, and rise up!
